mainTopic: Lenient evidence for letting an עגונה remarry: a גוי's offhand remark, a בת קול, one witness, and a woman's testimony
overview: The amud opens by finishing a story about a woman whose husband's death was reported by a גוי. רב יוסף rules from a ברייתא that a גוי with a motive, like a fruit seller praising his goods, is not believed. Three stories then show a גוי who mentions a death innocently, out of sadness, and is believed. A new משנה lets a woman remarry based on testimony by dim light, or on a voice whose speaker cannot be seen. The גמרא shows this follows בית הלל. It then asks whether the voice might have come from a שד, settling the question with a 'shadow of a shadow', and whether it might have been a scheming צרה. The next משנה tells how a tradition from רבן גמליאל הזקן allowed remarriage based on one witness, and how the practice spread to weaker witnesses. רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע disagree, and רבי עקיבא excludes a woman, a slave and relatives. The גמרא explains that רבי עקיבא's position changed once the practice was established. The amud ends with the innkeeper story, which רבי עקיבא answers by pointing to her physical proof.

steps.title: The woman is sent to רב יוסף
steps.stepSummary: After the woman waited three רגלים with no ruling, רב אדא בר אהבה tells her to bring her case to רב יוסף, known for his sharp mind.
steps.simpleTranslation: For three Festivals. רב אדא בר אהבה said to her: Go before רב יוסף, whose knife is sharp.
steps.whatsHappening: The story, which began before this section, continues. The woman still has no answer, so she is sent to a different great רב. This sets up the ruling that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her question is whether she may remarry based on a גוי's report that her husband died. It stayed unresolved for three רגלים. Calling רב יוסף's 'knife sharp' tells us he is the right person to cut through this hard case.

keyTerms.meaning: Go before him (to ask your question)
His knife is sharp, meaning he has a sharp, clear mind for פסק

phrases.english: for three Festivals.
phrases.notes: This picks up in the middle of the story. Her case had been left waiting through three רגלים without an answer.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לַהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said to her:
Go before Rav Yosef,
whose knife is sharp.
phrases.notes: It's a figure of speech: his mind cuts straight through tough questions.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לַהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: זִיל לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of the woman's case from the previous section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The unresolved case of a גוי's report of a husband's death is brought to רב יוסף.

steps.title: רב יוסף rules from the case of the fruit seller
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף settles the case from a ברייתא. A גוי who says his fruit is ערלה, from עזיקה, or נטע רבעי is not believed, because he only wants to make his goods look better.
steps.simpleTranslation: She went before him. He resolved it from this ברייתא: A גוי was selling fruit in the market and said, 'These fruits are ערלה,' or 'They are from עזיקה,' or 'They are נטע רבעי.' He has said nothing, because he only meant to make his merchandise look better.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the woman's question by quoting a ברייתא about a גוי selling fruit. The ברייתא says we ignore what the גוי says when he has a reason to say it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling the fruit ערלה, עזיקה, or רבעי would normally make it forbidden. Here it does not, because the seller is just advertising and has a motive. רב יוסף learns that a גוי who speaks with an agenda is not believed. He applies this to the woman's case, so the גוי's report there is not relied on.

keyTerms.meaning: Fruit from a tree's first three years, which is forbidden
Produce from land worked during שמיטה
Fourth-year fruit, which is eaten only in ירושלים
To make his merchandise look better

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not saying the fruit is definitely fine for some other reason. It is only saying the גוי's words carry no weight, because he had a selling motive.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the key line for this whole topic: a גוי with an agenda is not believed. The stories that follow show the other side, an innocent remark that is accepted.

phrases.english: She went before him.
He resolved it from this baraita:
A gentile who was selling fruit in the market,
and said: 'These fruits are orla,'
'they are from Azeka,'
'they are fourth-year produce' —
he has said nothing,
he intended only to enhance his merchandise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רב יוסף's answer to the case that was brought to him in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: Whether a גוי's statement can be relied on in the woman's case.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of the גוי selling fruit, whose words are ignored because he has a motive.

steps.title: אבא יודן's story: the Jew who died on the road
steps.stepSummary: אבא יודן איש צידן tells of a גוי who sadly said that his Jewish travel companion died and that he buried him. Based on that, the wife was allowed to remarry.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא יודן איש צידן said: There was an incident with a Jew and a גוי who traveled together. The גוי came and said, 'Alas for the Jew who was with me on the road, for he died on the road and I buried him.' And they allowed his wife to remarry.
steps.whatsHappening: The same ברייתא continues with a real-life story. In it, a גוי's report of a death was accepted, and the widow was allowed to remarry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the גוי is not selling or arguing for anything. He is simply sighing over what happened ('חבל על...'). With no agenda, his words count. This is the opposite of the fruit seller.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident (a real case that happened)
And they allowed his wife to marry
Speaking offhandedly, innocently, with no motive

phrases.english: Abba Yudan of Sidon said:
An incident with a Jew and a gentile
who traveled on the road,
and the gentile came and said:
'Alas for the Jew
who was with me on the road,
for he died on the road, and I buried him,'
and they allowed his wife to marry.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּא יוּדָן אִישׁ צַיְידָן אָמַר: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל וְגוֹי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא. It moves from a גוי with a motive, who is not believed, to a גוי speaking innocently, who is believed.
steps.raayaObject: That a גוי's offhand report of a death is enough to let the wife remarry.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The real case reported by אבא יודן איש צידן.

steps.title: Second story: the chained prisoners going to Antioch
steps.stepSummary: A group of prisoners in neck-collars was being led to Antioch. A גוי sadly said they died and he buried them, and their wives were allowed to remarry.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another incident: a chained group of people was walking to Antioch. A certain גוי came and said, 'Alas for the chained group of people, for they died and I buried them.' And they allowed their wives to remarry.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a second story with the same pattern. A whole group is reported dead by a גוי speaking sadly, and all the wives may remarry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once again the גוי is only lamenting, not trying to gain anything. This story shows the rule works even for many people at once, not just one traveler.

phrases.aramaic: וְשׁוּב מַעֲשֶׂה בְּקוֹלָר שֶׁל בְּנֵי אָדָם,
phrases.english: And another incident with a collared group of people,
phrases.notes: These were prisoners, each one chained by a collar around the neck.

phrases.english: who were walking to Antioch,
and a certain gentile came and said:
'Alas for the collared group of people,
for they died, and I buried them,'
and they allowed their wives to marry.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשׁוּב מַעֲשֶׂה בְּקוֹלָר שֶׁל בְּנֵי אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second example with the same pattern as step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That an offhand report by a גוי lets wives remarry, even for a group.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The incident of the collared prisoners going to Antioch.

steps.title: Third story: the sixty men going to ביתר
steps.stepSummary: Sixty men were walking to the siege of ביתר. A גוי sadly said they died and he buried them, and their wives were allowed to remarry.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another incident: sixty people were walking to the siege of ביתר. A גוי came and said, 'Alas for the sixty people who were walking on the road to ביתר, for they died and I buried them.' And they allowed their wives to remarry.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends its list with a third story of the same kind. The wives of sixty men are permitted based on a grieving remark by a גוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three stories in a row make the pattern very clear. When a גוי mentions a death in passing, out of sadness, the חכמים rely on it. Together with the fruit seller, this gives the full picture: a motive cancels his word, and innocent speech makes it count.
steps.whatToRemember: A גוי who has a motive (like the fruit seller) is not believed. A גוי who mentions a death offhandedly, in sadness, with no agenda (מסיח לפי תומו) is believed, and the wives may remarry.
steps.whyThisMatters: These stories are the basis for the הלכה that a wife may remarry based on a גוי's innocent, offhand report of her husband's death.

phrases.english: And another incident with sixty people
who were walking to the siege of Beitar,
and a gentile came and said:
'Alas for sixty people
who were walking on the road to Beitar,
for they died, and I buried them,'
and they allowed their wives to marry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The third and final example in the ברייתא's series of stories.
steps.raayaObject: That a גוי's offhand report of death is accepted to let wives remarry.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The incident of the sixty men on the road to ביתר.

steps.title: The משנה: testimony by dim light and by a voice
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that witnesses may testify about a death even if they saw the body only by candlelight or moonlight. A woman may also remarry based on a בת קול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Witnesses may testify by candlelight and by moonlight. And the court may let a woman remarry based on a voice heard from someone who cannot be seen.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists two more kinds of evidence that are good enough to let a woman remarry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally we might worry that dim light is not enough to recognize a face. The משנה says it is enough. It also accepts a voice announcing a death even when no one can see who is speaking. Both rulings follow the general leniency in עדות אשה, which runs through this whole פרק.

keyTerms.meaning: They testify (here, that a man is dead)
The court allows (a woman) to remarry
A voice heard from someone who cannot be seen

steps.confusionAlert: Here בת קול does not mean a voice from Heaven. It means a voice whose speaker is out of sight.

phrases.english: MISHNA: They may testify by candlelight
phrases.notes: They are testifying that they saw the man's dead body.

phrases.english: and by moonlight,
and they allow a woman to remarry based on a disembodied voice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה that continues the theme of lenient evidence for an עגונה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Testimony based on candlelight or moonlight is valid. A woman may remarry based on a בת קול announcing her husband's death.

steps.title: The story of the voice on the mountain top
steps.stepSummary: Someone on a mountain top announced that a certain man had died. When people went up, no one was there. The woman was still allowed to remarry.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a case of someone who stood on top of a mountain and said: 'So-and-so, son of so-and-so, from such-and-such a place, died.' They went up and found no person there. Even so, they allowed his wife to remarry.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה backs up its ruling about a בת קול with a real story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story is the clearest kind of בת קול: a voice, and then no speaker can be found. Even so, the חכמים relied on it. That shows the rule in action.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident; a real case that happened
So-and-so; a certain person or place

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּאֶחָד שֶׁעָמַד עַל רֹאשׁ הָהָר
phrases.english: There was an incident with someone who stood on top of the mountain
and said: 'So-and-so, son of so-and-so,
from such-and-such a place, died.'
They went and did not find a person there,
and they allowed his wife to remarry.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּאֶחָד שֶׁעָמַד עַל רֹאשׁ הָהָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that supports the בת קול ruling of Step 6.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a woman may remarry based on a בת קול.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The incident of the voice on the mountain top, where no speaker was found.

steps.title: The story in צלמון of the man bitten by a snake
steps.stepSummary: In צלמון, a man said who he was and that a snake had bitten him and he was dying. People could not recognize him afterward, but they still let his wife remarry.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another case happened in צלמון. A man said: 'I am so-and-so, son of so-and-so. A snake bit me, and I am dying.' They went and could not recognize him. Even so, they went ahead and allowed his wife to remarry.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a second story. This time the dying man reports his own death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the only identification is the man's own words. The body itself could not be recognized. The חכמים still relied on what he said, so what a dying person says about himself can be enough.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה accepts weak evidence to let an עגונה remarry: dim light, a voice with no visible speaker, or a dying man naming himself.

phrases.english: And there was another incident in צלמון,

phrases.aramaic: בְּאֶחָד שֶׁאָמַר: ״אֲנִי אִישׁ פְּלוֹנִי בֶּן אִישׁ פְּלוֹנִי,
phrases.english: with someone who said: 'I am so-and-so, son of so-and-so;
a snake bit me, and I am dying.'
And they went and did not recognize him,
and they went and allowed his wife to remarry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second supporting story for the משנה's lenient rulings.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a woman may remarry based on a statement whose speaker cannot be identified by sight.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The incident in צלמון of the man bitten by a snake.

steps.title: A ברייתא: בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about a בת קול
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר שמואל quotes a ברייתא. בית שמאי say a woman may not remarry based on a בת קול, and בית הלל say she may.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר שמואל said: It was taught in a ברייתא that בית שמאי say a woman may not remarry based on a בת קול, and בית הלל say she may.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and brings a ברייתא showing that the משנה's ruling about a בת קול was a מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה stated the lenient rule without naming anyone who disagreed. This ברייתא shows that בית שמאי disagreed and that the משנה follows בית הלל.

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר שְׁמוּאֵל: תָּנָא,
phrases.english: GEMARA: רבה בר שמואל said: It was taught:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: אֵין מַשִּׂיאִין עַל פִּי בַּת קוֹל.
phrases.english: בית שמאי say: They do not allow a woman to remarry based on a disembodied voice.

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: מַשִּׂיאִין עַל פִּי בַּת קוֹל.
phrases.english: And בית הלל say: They do allow a woman to remarry based on a disembodied voice.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא showing that the משנה's בת קול ruling was a מחלוקת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי forbid remarriage based on a בת קול, and בית הלל permit it.

steps.title: Why did רבה בר שמואל need to teach this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what this ברייתא adds. Our משנה already rules that a woman may remarry based on a בת קול.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he teaching us? This is already our משנה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבה בר שמואל. His ברייתא seems to teach nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the הלכה follows בית הלל, and our משנה already rules leniently, the practical rule is already known. So why quote the ברייתא at all?

keyTerms.meaning: What is he teaching us (that is new)?

phrases.english: What is he teaching us?
It is our משנה!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן, מַתְנִיתִין הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether Step 9 adds anything beyond the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה בר שמואל's statement in Step 9.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The practical ruling is already stated in our משנה, so the ברייתא seems unnecessary.

steps.title: An unnamed strict source follows בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: The answer: if we ever find an unnamed source saying a woman may not remarry based on a בת קול, we should know it follows בית שמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he teaches us: if you find an unnamed source that says they do not allow remarriage based on a בת קול, it is בית שמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The ברייתא tells us who stands behind any strict unnamed ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new point is not the הלכה itself. It is how to treat a strict unnamed source. Such a source is בית שמאי's view, so we do not follow it.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he is teaching us

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a common use of a ברייתא: it identifies whose view an unnamed source follows, so we know whether that source is the accepted הלכה.

phrases.english: This is what he teaches us:
that if you find an unnamed source saying they do not allow her to remarry,
it is בית שמאי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the purpose of the ברייתא: it identifies whose view an unnamed source follows.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to only repeat our משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: It teaches that any unnamed strict ruling about a בת קול is בית שמאי's view and is not followed.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows בית הלל, and an unnamed strict source on this question follows בית שמאי.

steps.title: Maybe the voice on the mountain was a שד
steps.stepSummary: Going back to the mountain story, the גמרא asks: since no person was found there, maybe the voice came from a שד.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says 'they went and did not find' anyone. But maybe it was a שד!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the mountain story in the משנה. It raises a worry about how the חכמים could rely on that voice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If no human was found, the speaker may not have been human at all. A שד's announcement would mean nothing. So how could the חכמים let the wife remarry?

phrases.english: 'And they went and did not find' anyone.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the mountain story from the משנה (Step 7).

phrases.english: But perhaps it was a demon?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָלְכוּ וְלֹא מָצְאוּ. וְדִלְמָא שֵׁד הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the mountain story of Step 7 to question it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling in the mountain story (Step 7).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A voice with no speaker found may have come from a שד, and that would not be trustworthy.

steps.title: They saw a human form
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting רב, answers that they saw the speaker had the form of a person.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: They saw that he had the form of a person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the worry about a שד. The people saw a human-looking figure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story is narrowed. It was not a voice with nothing seen at all; they saw a figure with the form of a person.

phrases.english: רב יהודה said that רב said:
That they saw he had the form of a person.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: שֶׁרָאוּ לוֹ דְּמוּת אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the case: a human shape was seen.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Nothing was seen, so the voice could have been a שד.
steps.terutzMaskana: They saw a human form, so they assumed it was a person.

steps.title: But שדים can look like people too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that שדים can also look like people, so seeing a human form proves nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: They, the שדים, also look like people!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a שד can take on a human appearance, seeing a human shape does not rule out a שד. So the first answer is not enough.

phrases.english: They too look like people!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's answer that they saw a human form.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שדים can also appear in human form, so a human form does not prove the speaker was a person.

steps.title: They saw that he cast a shadow
steps.stepSummary: The answer: they saw that the figure had a shadow (בבואה), which shows it was a real person.
steps.simpleTranslation: They saw that he had a shadow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer: the figure cast a shadow. The very next step challenges this answer too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer assumes that a שד, even one that looks human, has no shadow, so seeing a shadow would prove the speaker was a person. Step 16 challenges exactly that assumption, since שדים do have a shadow.

keyTerms.meaning: That they saw for him (that he had)

phrases.english: That they saw he had a shadow.
phrases.notes: For now the גמרא assumes a שד has no shadow. The next step questions that.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a detail that tells a person apart from a שד.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A human form alone could still have been a שד.
steps.terutzMaskana: The figure cast a shadow, which at this stage is assumed to prove it was a person.

steps.title: Demons also have shadows
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that a shadow proves nothing, since שדים also cast shadows.
steps.simpleTranslation: But they (the שדים) also have a shadow!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last answer. Seeing a shadow cannot prove the speaker was human, because שדים have shadows too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 used the shadow to tell a person apart from a שד. This step says the test fails, because both have shadows. So we are back to not knowing who spoke.

phrases.english: But they too have a shadow!
phrases.notes: "They" means the שדים from the earlier steps.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 15
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A sign found in both people and שדים cannot tell them apart.

steps.title: They saw a shadow of a shadow
steps.stepSummary: The answer: they saw a shadow of a shadow, which only a real person has.
steps.simpleTranslation: They saw that he had a shadow of a shadow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a stronger sign. They saw not just a shadow but a shadow of a shadow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer keeps the shadow idea but makes it sharper. A plain shadow is shared by people and שדים. A shadow of a shadow is claimed to belong only to people.

phrases.english: Where they saw that he had a shadow of a shadow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 16
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case to a more specific sign
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any shadow proves it was a person
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a shadow of a shadow proves it was a person

steps.title: Maybe demons have a shadow of a shadow too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: perhaps שדים also have a shadow of a shadow.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps they also have a shadow of a shadow?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes again. Maybe שדים have even this double shadow, so the new sign proves nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same attack as Step 16, now aimed at the sharper sign. Unless we know שדים lack a shadow of a shadow, the proof still fails.

phrases.english: But perhaps they themselves
also have a shadow of a shadow.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִלְמָא לְדִידְהוּ אִית לְהוּ בָּבוּאָה דְבָבוּאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 17
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without knowing what שדים lack, no sign can rule them out.

steps.title: Testimony that demons lack a shadow of a shadow
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא reports that יונתן שידא told him: שדים have a shadow but not a shadow of a shadow.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: יונתן the שד-expert told me, they have a shadow, but they do not have a shadow of a shadow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the question with a report from someone who knew about שדים. They have a shadow, but not a shadow of a shadow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This closes the שד line of questions. Step 17's sign really works, so the voice on the mountain came from a real person.

keyTerms.meaning: the אמורא who reports the information

steps.whatToRemember: The שד worry is fully answered: a shadow of a shadow shows the speaker was a real person.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina said:
Yonatan the demon expert said to me:
A shadow, they have;
a shadow of a shadow, they do not have.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא, אָמַר לִי יוֹנָתָן שֵׁידָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 18 and backs up Step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: A factual report from an expert
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שדים might have a shadow of a shadow
steps.terutzMaskana: שדים do not have a shadow of a shadow, so the sign proves a human speaker

steps.title: Maybe it was a rival wife
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a new worry: maybe the voice was a צרה trying to trick the woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps it was a rival wife?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know a real person spoke, the גמרא asks if that person could have been lying, for example a צרה who wanted the woman to remarry wrongly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question moves from what the speaker was to whether the speaker can be trusted. Even a real human voice might be a trick by someone who hates the woman.

keyTerms.meaning: a rival wife, married to the same husband

phrases.english: But perhaps it was a rival wife?
phrases.notes: The worry is that an enemy shouted the news on purpose, so the woman would remarry while her husband is alive.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge now that the שד question is closed
steps.kashyaTarget: Trusting the unknown speaker on the mountain
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Someone with a motive to harm the woman could make up the report.

steps.title: In times of danger we are not so suspicious
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי ישמעאל taught that in a time of danger a גט may be written and given even without recognizing the husband. The same easier approach applies here.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: in a time of danger, we write and give a גט even though the witnesses do not recognize the husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. In unusual, dangerous situations we do not raise every possible suspicion, so we do not worry about a צרה here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a גט needs witnesses who know the husband, to rule out a faker. In danger we drop that worry. The mountain case is treated the same way, so the far-fetched idea of a scheming צרה is set aside.

keyTerms.meaning: the school of רבי ישמעאל taught (a ברייתא)

steps.whatToRemember: In emergency-type situations חז״ל do not raise every suspicion. This is why the mountain voice is trusted.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
During a period of danger
one may write and give (a bill of divorce),
even though they do not recognize (the husband).

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: בִּשְׁעַת הַסַּכָּנָה כּוֹתְבִין וְנוֹתְנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the צרה challenge of Step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: Comparison to an existing rule (time of danger)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every possible deception must be ruled out
steps.terutzMaskana: In danger-like situations we do not worry about unlikely deceptions

steps.title: רבי עקיבא meets נחמיה in נהרדעא
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: רבי עקיבא tells how נחמיה איש בית דלי asked him whether only יהודה בן בבא allows remarriage based on one witness, and רבי עקיבא said yes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said: When I went down to נהרדעא to make the year a leap year, נחמיה איש בית דלי found me. He said: I heard that in ארץ ישראל they do not let a woman remarry based on one witness, except יהודה בן בבא. I told him: That is right.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a story from רבי עקיבא. This step sets up the background before the main message in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We learn that in ארץ ישראל, permitting a woman to remarry on one witness's word was held only by יהודה בן בבא, a lone opinion. נחמיה checks this fact first, because his message depends on it.

keyTerms.meaning: to make the year a leap year

phrases.english: MISHNA: Rabbi Akiva said:
When I went down to Neharde'a
to make the year a leap year,
Neḥemya of Beit D'li found me.
He said to me: I heard
that they do not let a woman remarry

phrases.aramaic: בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל פִּי עֵד אֶחָד
phrases.english: in Eretz Yisrael based on a single witness,
except for Yehuda ben Bava.
And I told him: That is so.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אָמַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: כְּשֶׁיָּרַדְתִּי לִנְהַרְדְּעָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the גמרא's discussion ends
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In ארץ ישראל only יהודה בן בבא allowed remarriage based on one witness.

steps.title: נחמיה's tradition from רבן גמליאל הזקן
steps.stepSummary: נחמיה asks רבי עקיבא to tell the חכמים in his name that he has a tradition from רבן גמליאל הזקן: a woman may remarry based on one witness.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to me: Tell them in my name: you know the land is thrown into confusion by army troops. I received from רבן גמליאל הזקן that a woman may remarry based on one witness.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the main message of the story. נחמיה sends a tradition supporting the lenient view, explaining he cannot come himself because of the soldiers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נחמיה adds a second voice to יהודה בן בבא's view, and it comes with a tradition from an earlier great teacher, רבן גמליאל הזקן. The line about troops explains why the message is sent through רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: the elder רבן גמליאל, of an earlier generation

phrases.english: He said to me: Tell them in my name:
phrases.notes: "Them" means the חכמים back in ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: You know
that the country is thrown into confusion by army troops,
I received a tradition from Rabban Gamliel the Elder

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמַּשִּׂיאִין אֶת הָאִשָּׁה עַל פִּי עֵד אֶחָד.
phrases.english: that we may let a woman remarry based on a single witness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Delivers the message that Step 22 set up
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a tradition from רבן גמליאל הזקן that a woman may remarry based on one witness.
steps.whyThisMatters: This tradition is the source for the well-known rule that one witness is enough to permit an עגונה to remarry.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל rejoices at the support
steps.stepSummary: When רבי עקיבא reported this to רבן גמליאל, he was happy and said: we have found a companion for רבי יהודה בן בבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: When I came and told these things before רבן גמליאל, he was happy with my words and said: We have found a companion for רבי יהודה בן בבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends. רבן גמליאל is glad that the lenient view now has a second supporter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, רבי יהודה בן בבא stood alone, and a lone opinion is hard to rely on. Now נחמיה, backed by a tradition from רבן גמליאל הזקן, agrees with him. So the lenient view gains real weight.
steps.whatToRemember: One witness permitting a woman to remarry is no longer a lone opinion. It has a supporter and an old tradition behind it.
steps.confusionAlert: There are two different people called רבן גמליאל here. רבן גמליאל הזקן gave the old tradition, and a later רבן גמליאל heard the report and rejoiced.

phrases.english: And when I came and presented the matter
before Rabban Gamliel,
he rejoiced at my words and said:

phrases.aramaic: מָצָאנוּ חָבֵר לְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בָּבָא.
phrases.english: We have found a companion for Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְשֶׁבָּאתִי וְהִרְצֵיתִי הַדְּבָרִים לִפְנֵי רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how the message from Step 23 was received
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The lenient view (one witness is enough) is now backed by more than one sage and can be relied on.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל remembers the case of תל ארזא
steps.stepSummary: While discussing this, רבן גמליאל remembers that men had been killed in תל ארזא, and he then lets their wives remarry based on one witness.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a result of this conversation, רבן גמליאל remembered that people had been killed in תל ארזא, and רבן גמליאל allowed their wives to remarry based on one witness.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues the story from before. Hearing נחמיה's tradition reminds רבן גמליאל of men killed in תל ארזא, and he now acts on the tradition by letting their wives remarry on one witness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now we had only a tradition from רבן גמליאל הזקן and a lone opinion. Now רבן גמליאל puts it into practice in a real case. That makes the rule of one witness an actual ruling, not just a view.

keyTerms.meaning: As a result of this matter or conversation

phrases.english: As a result of this matter,
phrases.notes: He means the report from רבי עקיבא about נחמיה's tradition, which we just saw.

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel remembered
that people were killed in Tel Arza,
and Rabban Gamliel allowed their wives to remarry
based on one witness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's story: after hearing the tradition, רבן גמליאל remembers acting on it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Prompted by the tradition, רבן גמליאל allowed the wives of the men killed in תל ארזא to remarry based on one witness.

steps.title: The practice spreads to weaker kinds of witnesses
steps.stepSummary: From then on, the practice became to allow remarriage even based on hearsay, or on the word of a slave, a woman, or a maidservant.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they became established to allow remarriage based on a witness repeating what another witness said, or on the word of a slave, a woman, or a maidservant.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells us what happened after רבן גמליאל's ruling. The courts began accepting testimony that would normally not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This goes beyond one witness. Hearsay, slaves, and women are normally not valid witnesses in court, but for a woman's remarriage they were now accepted. This 'established practice' (הוחזקו) becomes important in the גמרא later.

keyTerms.meaning: They became established; it became the accepted practice
Hearsay: a witness repeating what another witness said

phrases.english: And they became established to allow remarriage
based on a witness from the mouth of a witness,

phrases.aramaic: מִפִּי עֶבֶד, מִפִּי אִשָּׁה, מִפִּי שִׁפְחָה.
phrases.english: from the mouth of a slave, from the mouth of a woman, from the mouth of a maidservant.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Describes the lasting result of רבן גמליאל's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The accepted practice became to let a woman remarry even based on hearsay, a slave, a woman, or a maidservant.
steps.whyThisMatters: The word הוחזקו, 'they established,' is the key to how the גמרא answers its question about רבי עקיבא in step 30.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע reject one witness
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע disagree and say a woman may not remarry based on only one witness.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע say: We do not allow a woman to remarry based on one witness.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now brings a dissenting opinion. These two תנאים do not accept the easier approach at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their view goes back to the normal rule that testimony needs two witnesses. In their view, even one fully valid witness is not enough here, so certainly not the weaker witnesses listed before.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not allow (her) to remarry

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua say:
We do not allow the woman to remarry
based on one witness.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the practice of relying on one witness.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע, one witness is not enough for a woman to remarry.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא excludes women, slaves, and relatives
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says a woman may not remarry based on the word of a woman, a slave, a maidservant, or relatives.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: Not based on a woman, not based on a slave, not based on a maidservant, and not based on relatives.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a middle opinion. רבי עקיבא does not reject one witness, but he limits who that witness can be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא does not join רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע in rejecting one witness. He only limits who that witness can be: someone who could normally testify, so a woman, slave, maidservant, or relative does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: Relatives, who are normally not valid witnesses

steps.confusionAlert: רבי עקיבא is NOT saying one witness is invalid. He accepts one witness. He only rejects these specific kinds of witnesses.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא עַל פִּי אִשָּׁה, וְלֹא עַל פִּי עֶבֶד,
phrases.english: Not based on a woman, and not based on a slave,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא עַל פִּי שִׁפְחָה, וְלֹא עַל פִּי קְרוֹבִים.
phrases.english: and not based on a maidservant, and not based on relatives.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: לֹא עַל פִּי אִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third view: accepts one witness but limits the expansion described in step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא accepts one witness, but not a woman, slave, maidservant, or relative.
steps.whatToRemember: Three views in the משנה: the established practice accepts even weak witnesses; רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע need more than one witness; רבי עקיבא accepts one valid witness only.

steps.title: Does רבי עקיבא really not trust a woman?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי עקיבא's view from a ברייתא where he argues that a woman is trusted to say her husband died.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי עקיבא really hold that a woman's word does not count? But a ברייתא teaches: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says in the name of רבי עקיבא: A woman is trusted to bring her own גט, based on a קל וחומר. If women whom the חכמים said are not trusted to say 'her husband died' are still trusted to bring their גט, then this woman, who is trusted to say 'her husband died,' should certainly be trusted to bring her own גט. This shows that only the women the חכמים listed are not trusted; a woman in general is trusted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a challenge to רבי עקיבא in our משנה. It quotes him in a ברייתא where he seems to trust a woman to report a husband's death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, רבי עקיבא builds a קל וחומר that takes for granted that some women are trusted to say a husband died. The only women not trusted are the specific ones the חכמים listed. So in general a woman is trusted, which goes against his statement in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: But a ברייתא teaches (introduces a contradiction)
An argument from a weaker case to a stronger case
To bring her own גט and testify about it

phrases.english: Gemara:

phrases.aramaic: וְסָבַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא עַל פִּי אִשָּׁה לָא?
phrases.english: And does Rabbi Akiva hold that based on a woman, no?
But isn't it taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says in the name of Rabbi Akiva:
A woman is trusted to bring her own bill of divorce
based on a kal vachomer;
If women whom the Sages said
are not trusted to say 'her husband died'
phrases.notes: These are women like her rival wife, whom the חכמים listed earlier as not trusted about her husband.

phrases.english: are trusted to bring their bills of divorce,
this one, who is trusted to say 'her husband died',
isn't it logical that she is trusted to bring her bill of divorce?

phrases.aramaic: נָשִׁים שֶׁאָמְרוּ חֲכָמִים הוּא דְּלָא מְהֵימְנִי,
phrases.english: It is the women whom the Sages mentioned who are not believed,
but a woman in general is believed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא עַל פִּי אִשָּׁה לָא? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי עקיבא's ruling in the משנה from his own words in a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's statement that a woman's testimony is not accepted for remarriage (step 28).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי עקיבא's קל וחומר in the ברייתא assumes that most women are trusted to say a husband died, and only certain listed women are not. That contradicts his saying 'not based on a woman.'

steps.title: Before and after the practice was established
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי עקיבא's rejection of a woman was before the practice became established, and his trusting a woman was after.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult. Here, it was before they established the practice; there, it was after they established the practice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by placing the two statements of רבי עקיבא at two different times.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי עקיבא spoke before the practice of accepting a woman's testimony took hold (step 26). Once it became established, he accepted it too, as the ברייתא shows. So he did not contradict himself; the practice changed in between.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא's two statements fit together: before the practice was established he did not trust a woman, and after it was established he did.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
here, it was before they established,
phrases.notes: 'Here' is our משנה. 'Established' points back to the word הוחזקו in step 26.

phrases.english: there, it was after they established.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting by time: two statements made before and after a change in practice.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי עקיבא contradicts himself about trusting a woman.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is from before the practice was established; the ברייתא is from after, when רבי עקיבא also accepted a woman.

steps.title: The story of the Levites and the innkeeper
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: the חכמים tell רבי עקיבא about Levites whose friend died at an inn, and his wife was allowed to remarry based on the innkeeper's word.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: There was a story with Levites who went to צוער, the city of date palms. One of them got sick, and they brought him to an inn. When they came back, they asked the innkeeper, 'Where is our friend?' She told them, 'He died, and I buried him.' And they allowed his wife to remarry.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. The חכמים answer רבי עקיבא with a real story where a woman's report of death was accepted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא said a woman's word is not enough. The חכמים bring a past case where the only witness was a woman, the innkeeper, and still the wife was allowed to remarry. The story is their evidence; the argument comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident; a real story brought as evidence

phrases.english: Mishna:
They said to him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רבי עקיבא, answering what he said in the last משנה.

phrases.english: There was an incident with Levites
who went to Tzoar, the city of date palms,
and one of them became sick,
and they brought him to an inn.
And on their return they said to the innkeeper:
'Where is our friend?'
She said to them: 'He died, and I buried him,'
and they allowed his wife to remarry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the גמרא's discussion, a new משנה continues the debate with רבי עקיבא from step 28.
steps.raayaObject: That a woman's report of death can be enough for the wife to remarry, against רבי עקיבא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A past case where the wife of a Levite was allowed to remarry based on an innkeeper's words.

steps.title: Shouldn't a respectable woman be trusted like the innkeeper?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים argue: if an innkeeper was trusted, a כהנת should certainly be trusted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And should a כהנת not be like the innkeeper?
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים finish their challenge to רבי עקיבא by drawing a conclusion from the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If an innkeeper, not an especially trusted person, was believed, then certainly a respectable woman like a כהנת should be believed. So a woman's word should count, against רבי עקיבא's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: A כהן's daughter or wife; a respectable woman

phrases.english: And should a priestess not be like an innkeeper?
phrases.notes: A כהנת is a respectable woman. They mean any proper Jewish woman should be trusted at least as much as the innkeeper.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the argument out of the story in step 31.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's ruling that a woman's testimony is not accepted (step 28).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר-style argument: if an innkeeper was trusted, a respectable woman should surely be trusted too.

steps.title: The innkeeper was believed because she had physical proof
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא rejects the חכמים' proof. The innkeeper was not believed on her word alone. She brought out the man's staff, bag, and ספר תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said to them: When a woman is like the innkeeper, she will be believed. The innkeeper brought out to them his staff, his bag, and the ספר תורה that he had with him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא answers the חכמים by showing that the innkeeper case is different. She had physical evidence that backed up her story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים argued that if an innkeeper was trusted, a כהנת surely should be. רבי עקיבא says the innkeeper's word was never trusted alone. The dead man's belongings supported it, so this case does not prove that a woman's plain statement is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Innkeeper (a woman who runs an inn)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא does not deny that the innkeeper was believed. He says she was believed because her word came with proof: the dead man's own belongings.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read רבי עקיבא as saying a woman can never be believed. He is saying a woman is believed when she has supporting evidence like the innkeeper had.

phrases.english: He said to them: When she is like the innkeeper, she is believed.
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי עקיבא, answering the חכמים from the previous step.

phrases.english: The innkeeper brought out to them
his staff and his bag
and the Torah scroll that was in his hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof and the קל וחומר the חכמים built from the innkeeper story.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the innkeeper case. It does not show that a woman's plain word is accepted.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The innkeeper's testimony was backed by physical evidence (staff, bag, ספר תורה), so it was not testimony alone.
